1 Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and spoke, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.1 2 In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and in. Yahweh said to you, ‘You will be shepherd of my people Israel, and you will be prince over Israel.’”2345 3 So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed6 David king over Israel.78✦ 4 David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.9 5 In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.10✦ 6 The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land11, who spoke to David, saying, “The blind and the lame will keep you out of here,” thinking, “David can’t come in here.”12✦ 7 Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion13. This is David’s city.14✦ 8 David said on that day15, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him go up to the watercourse and strike those lame and blind, who are hated by David’s soul16.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame can’t come into the house.”1718✦ 9 David lived in the stronghold, and called it David’s city. David built around from Millo and inward.1920✦ 10 David grew greater and greater, for Yahweh, the God21 of Armies, was with him.2223 11 Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar trees, carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.242526✦ 12 David perceived that Yahweh had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.27 13 David took more concubines and wives for himself out of Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.28 14 These are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,2930 15 Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,3132 16 Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.333435 17 When the Philistines heard that they had anointed36 David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David, but David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.37✦ 18 Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.38✦ 19 David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?” Yahweh said to David, “Go up; for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into your hand.”3940✦ 20 David came to Baal Perazim, and David struck them there. Then he said, “Yahweh has broken my enemies before me, like the breach of waters41.” Therefore he called the name of that place Baal Perazim.424344✦ 21 They left their images there, and David and his men took them away.45✦ 22 The Philistines came up yet again and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.46✦ 23 When David inquired of Yahweh, he said, “You shall not go up. Circle around behind them, and attack them in front of the mulberry trees.4748✦ 24 When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then stir yourself up; for then Yahweh has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”4950✦ 25 David did so, as Yahweh commanded him, and struck the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.

123✦1 David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

4✦2 David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale Judah, to bring up from there God5’s ark, which is called by the Name, even the name of Yahweh of Armies who sits above the cherubim.678✦ 3 They set God9’s ark on a new cart, and brought it out of Abinadab’s house that was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.1011✦ 4 They brought it out of Abinadab’s house which was in the hill, with God12’s ark; and Ahio went before the ark.13✦ 5 David and all the house of Israel played before Yahweh with all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with castanets, and with cymbals.14151617✦ 6 When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached for God18’s ark and took hold of it, for the cattle stumbled.1920✦ 7 Yahweh’s anger burned against Uzzah, and God21 struck him there for his error; and he died there by God’s ark.2223✦ 8 David was displeased because Yahweh had broken out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez Uzzah to this day.2425✦ 9 David was afraid of Yahweh that day; and he said, “How could Yahweh’s ark come to me?”2627✦ 10 So David would not move Yahweh’s ark to be with him in David’s city; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.4041✦ 15 So David and all the house of Israel brought up Yahweh’s ark with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.4243✦ 16 As Yahweh’s ark came into David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before Yahweh; and she despised him in her heart44.4546✦ 17 They brought in Yahweh’s ark, and set it in its place in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace47 offerings before Yahweh.4849✦ 18 When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace50 offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh of Armies.5152 19 He gave to all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, both to men and women, to everyone a portion of bread, dates, and raisins. So all the people departed, each to his own house.53545556✦ 20 Then David returned to bless his household. Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, “How glorious the king of Israel was today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of his servants’ maids, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!”57✦ 21 David said to Michal, “It was before Yahweh, who chose me above your father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Yahweh, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before Yahweh.5859 22 I will be yet more undignified than this, and will be worthless in my own sight. But the maids of whom you have spoken will honor me.”60 23 Michal the daughter of Saul had no child61 to the day of her death.

11 When the king lived in his house, and Yahweh had given him rest from all his enemies all around,23 2 the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but God4’s ark dwells within curtains.”56✦ 3 Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your heart7, for Yahweh is with you.”89 4 That same night, Yahweh’s word came to Nathan, saying,1011✦ 5 “Go and tell my servant David, ‘Yahweh says, “Should you build me a house for me to dwell in?1213✦ 6 For I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought the children of Israel up out of Egypt, even to this day, but have moved around in a tent and in a tabernacle.14✦ 7 In all places in which I have walked with all the children of Israel, did I say a word to anyone from the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’”’15✦ 8 Now therefore tell my servant David this: ‘Yahweh of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people, over Israel.1617✦ 9 I have been with you wherever you went, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth18.1920✦ 10 I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not afflict them any more, as at the first,2122✦ 11 and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I will cause you to rest from all your enemies. Moreover Yahweh tells you that Yahweh will make you a house.2324✦ 12 When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will set up your offspring after you, who will proceed out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom.25✦ 13 He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever26.2728✦ 14 I will be his father, and he will be my son2930. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the children of men;3132✦ 15 but my loving kindness will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before you.3334✦ 16 Your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you. Your throne will be established forever.”’”3536✦ 17 Nathan spoke to David all these words, and according to all this vision.37✦ 18 Then David the king went in and sat before Yahweh; and he said, “Who am I, Lord Yahweh, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?3839404142✦ 19 This was yet a small thing in your eyes, Lord43 Yahweh, but you have spoken also of your servant’s house for a great while to come; and this among men, Lord Yahweh!444546✦ 20 What more can David say to you? For you know your servant, Lord47 Yahweh.4849✦ 21 For your word’s sake, and according to your own heart50, you have worked all this greatness, to make your servant know it.51✦ 22 Therefore you are great, Yahweh God52. For there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.535455✦ 23 What one nation in the earth56 is like your people, even like Israel, whom God57 went to redeem58 to himself for a people, and to make himself a name, and to do great things for you, and awesome things for your land, before your people, whom you redeemed to yourself out of Egypt, from the nations and their gods?59✦ 24 You established for yourself your people Israel to be your people forever; and you, Yahweh, became their God60.6162✦ 25 “Now, Yahweh God63, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as you have spoken.6465✦ 26 Let your name be magnified forever, saying, ‘Yahweh of Armies is God66 over Israel; and the house of your servant David will be established before you.’6768✦ 27 For you, Yahweh of Armies, the God69 of Israel, have revealed to your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found in his heart70 to pray this prayer to you.7172✦ 28 “Now, O Lord73 Yahweh, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.7475✦ 29 Now therefore, let it please you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, Lord76 Yahweh, have spoken it. 12✦1 After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued them; and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.34✦ 2 He defeated Moab, and measured them with the line5, making them to lie down on the ground6; and he measured two lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. The Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.7✦ 3 David also struck Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his dominion at the River.891011 4 David took from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand footmen. David hamstrung the chariot horses, but reserved enough of them for one hundred chariots.12✦ 5 When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty two thousand men of the Syrians.13✦ 6 Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.1415✦ 7 David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.16✦ 8 From Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.1718✦ 9 When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer,1920 10 then Toi sent Joram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him; for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. Joram brought with him vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze.212223✦ 11 King David also dedicated these to Yahweh, with the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations which he subdued—2425✦ 12 of Syria, of Moab, of the children of Ammon, of the Philistines, of Amalek, and of the plunder of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.26✦ 13 David earned a reputation when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand men of the Syrians in the Valley of Salt.27✦ 14 He put garrisons in Edom. Throughout all Edom, he put garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.2829✦ 15 David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness30 for all his people.31✦ 16 Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder,3233✦ 17 Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, Seraiah was scribe,343536✦ 18 Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief ministers.

1234✦1 David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan5’s sake?”6 2 There was of Saul’s house a servant whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David; and the king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” He said, “I am your servant.”78 3 The king said, “Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may show the kindness of God9 to him?” Ziba said to the king, “Jonathan still has a son, who is lame in his feet.”10✦ 4 The king said to him, “Where is he?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar.”11 5 Then King David sent and brought him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.12 6 Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, fell on his face, and showed respect. David said, “Mephibosheth?” He answered, “Behold, your servant!”13 7 David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land14 of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually15.”1617✦ 8 He bowed down, and said, “What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?”18✦ 9 Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said to him, “All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master’s son.19✦ 10 Till the land20 for him—you, your sons, and your servants. Bring in the harvest, that your master’s son may have bread to eat; but Mephibosheth your master’s son will always eat bread at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.21✦ 11 Then Ziba said to the king, “According to all that my lord22 the king commands his servant, so your servant will do.” So Mephibosheth ate at the king’s table like one of the king’s sons.23✦ 12 Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Mica. All who lived in Ziba’s house were servants to Mephibosheth.2425✦ 13 So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.

1✦1 After this, the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.23✦ 2 David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land4 of the children of Ammon.56✦ 3 But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord7, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn’t David sent his servants to you to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?”8✦ 4 So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off one half of their beards9, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.10✦ 5 When they told David this, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. The king said, “Wait at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”11✦ 6 When the children of Ammon saw that they had become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth Rehob and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.1213✦ 7 When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.14✦ 8 The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate. The Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the field.15✦ 9 Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel and put them in array against the Syrians.16✦ 10 The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.17✦ 11 He said, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.18✦ 12 Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people19 and for the cities of our God20; and may Yahweh do what seems good21 to him.”2223✦ 13 So Joab and the people who were with him came near to the battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him.24✦ 14 When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.25✦ 15 When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel, they gathered themselves together.26✦ 16 Hadadezer sent and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the River; and they came to Helam, with Shobach the captain of the army of Hadadezer at their head.27✦ 17 David was told that; and he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Syrians set themselves in array against David and fought with him.28✦ 18 The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed seven hundred charioteers of the Syrians and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their army, so that he died there.29✦ 19 When all the kings who were servants to Hadadezer saw that they were defeated before Israel, they made peace30 with Israel and served them. So the Syrians were afraid to help the children of Ammon any more.

1✦1 At the return of the year, at the time when kings go out2, David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.3✦ 2 At evening, David arose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof, he saw a woman4 bathing, and the woman was very beautiful to look at.56✦ 3 David sent and inquired after the woman7. One said, “Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, Uriah the Hittite’s wife?”8✦ 4 David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned to her house.9✦ 5 The woman10 conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, “I am with child.”11 6 David sent to Joab, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.12✦ 7 When Uriah had come to him, David asked him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.13 8 David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.14✦ 9 But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord15, and didn’t go down to his house.16 10 When they had told David, saying, “Uriah didn’t go down to his house,” David said to Uriah, “Haven’t you come from a journey? Why didn’t you go down to your house?”17 11 Uriah said to David, “The ark, Israel, and Judah, are staying in tents; and my lord18 Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open field. Shall I then go into my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul19 lives, I will not do this thing!”20✦ 12 David said to Uriah, “Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will let you depart.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next day.21 13 When David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk. At evening, he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord22, but didn’t go down to his house.23✦ 14 In the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.24 15 He wrote in the letter, saying, “Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck and die.”25 16 When Joab kept watch on the city, he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew that valiant men were.26 17 The men of the city went out and fought with Joab. Some of the people fell, even of David’s servants; and Uriah the Hittite died also.27 18 Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;28 19 and he commanded the messenger, saying, “When you have finished telling all the things concerning the war to the king,29 20 it shall be that, if the king’s wrath arise, and he asks you, ‘Why did you go so near to the city to fight? Didn’t you know that they would shoot from the wall?30✦ 21 Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Didn’t a woman31 cast an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?’ then you shall say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.’”3233✦ 22 So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.34 23 The messenger said to David, “The men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field; and we were on them even to the entrance of the gate.35 24 The shooters shot at your servants from off the wall; and some of the king’s servants are dead, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.”36 25 Then David said to the messenger, “Tell Joab, ‘Don’t let this thing displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Make your battle stronger against the city, and overthrow it.’ Encourage him.”37 26 When Uriah’s wife heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.38 27 When the mourning was past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Yahweh3940.

121 Yahweh sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city: the one rich, and the other poor.345✦ 2 The rich man6 had very many flocks and herds,7✦ 3 but the poor man8 had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him and with his children. It ate of his own food, drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.9✦ 4 A traveler came to the rich man10, and he didn’t want to take of his own flock and of his own herd to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”11✦ 5 David’s anger burned hot against the man12, and he said to Nathan, “As Yahweh lives, the man who has done this deserves to die!1314✦ 6 He must restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity!”15✦ 7 Nathan said to David, “You are the man161718! This is what Yahweh, the God19 of Israel, says: ‘I anointed20 you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.2122✦ 8 I gave you your master’s house and your master’s wives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that would have been too little, I would have added to you many more such things.23✦ 9 Why have you despised Yahweh’s word, to do that which is evil in his sight? You have struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, have taken his wife to be your wife, and have slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.2425✦ 10 Now therefore the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised me and have taken Uriah the Hittite’s wife to be your wife.’26✦ 11 “This is what Yahweh says: ‘Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.2728✦ 12 For you did this secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.’”29✦ 13 David said to Nathan, “I have sin30ned against Yahweh3132.” Nathan said to David, “Yahweh also has put away your sin. You will not die.333435✦ 14 However, because by this deed you have given great occasion to Yahweh’s enemies to blaspheme, the child also who is born to you will surely die.”3637✦ 15 Then Nathan departed to his house. Yahweh struck the child that Uriah’s wife bore to David, and he was very sick.3839✦ 16 David therefore begged God40 for the child; and David fasted, and went in and lay all night on the ground.4142✦ 17 The elders of his house arose beside him, to raise him up from the earth43; but he would not, and he didn’t eat bread with them.44✦ 18 On the seventh day, the child died. David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spoke to him and he didn’t listen to our voice. How will he then harm himself if we tell him that the child is dead?”45✦ 19 But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; and David said to his servants, “Is the child dead?” They said, “He is dead.”46✦ 20 Then David arose from the earth47, and washed and anointed48 himself, and changed his clothing; and he came into Yahweh’s house, and worshiped. Then he came to his own house; and when he requested, they set bread before him and he ate.4950✦ 21 Then his servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while he was alive, but when the child was dead, you rose up and ate bread.”51✦ 22 He said, “While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, ‘Who knows whether Yahweh will not be gracious to me, that the child may live?’5253✦ 23 But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”54✦ 24 David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her, and lay with her. She bore a son, and he called his name Solomon. Yahweh loved him;5556 25 and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he named him Jedidiah, for Yahweh’s sake.575859 26 Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.60✦ 27 Joab sent messengers to David, and said, “I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of waters61.62✦ 28 Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called by my name.”63✦ 29 David gathered all the people together and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and took it.64✦ 30 He took the crown of their king from off his head; and its weight was a talent of gold, and in it were precious stones; and it was set on David’s head. He brought a great quantity of plunder out of the city.6566✦ 31 He brought out the people who were in it, and put them to work under saws, under iron picks, under axes of iron, and made them go to the brick kiln; and he did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

12✦1 After this, Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar3; and Amnon the son of David loved her.4 2 Amnon was so troubled that he became sick because of his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her.5 3 But Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother; and Jonadab was a very subtle man6.789 4 He said to him, “Why, son of the king, are you so sad from day to day? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon said to him, “I love10 Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”11 5 Jonadab said to him, “Lay down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, tell him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it and eat it from her hand.’”12 6 So Amnon lay down and faked being sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.”13 7 Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, “Go now to your brother Amnon’s house, and prepare food for him.”14 8 So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was lying down. She took dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.15 9 She took the pan and poured them out before him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, “Have all men leave me.” Then every man16 went out from him.17 10 Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the room, that I may eat from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the room to Amnon her brother.18 11 When she had brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister!”19 12 She answered him, “No, my brother, do not force me! For no such thing ought to be done in Israel. Don’t you do this folly!20 13 As for me, where would I carry my shame? And as for you, you will be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from you.”21 14 However, he would not listen to her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her and lay with her.22 15 Then Amnon hated her with exceedingly great hatred; for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love23 with which he had loved her. Amnon said to her, “Arise, be gone!”24 16 She said to him, “Not so, because this great wrong in sending me away is worse than the other that you did to me!” But he would not listen to her.25 17 Then he called his servant who ministered to him, and said, “Now put this woman26 out from me, and bolt the door after her.”27 18 She had a garment of various colors on her, for the king’s daughters who were virgins dressed in such robes. Then his servant brought her out and bolted the door after her.28✦ 19 Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her garment of various colors that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head and went her way, crying aloud as she went.29✦ 20 Absalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now hold your peace30, my sister. He is your brother. Don’t take this thing to heart.” So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.31 21 But when King David heard of all these things, he was very angry32.33 22 Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good34 nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.35 23 After two full years, Absalom had sheep shearers in Baal Hazor, which is beside Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.3637✦ 24 Absalom came to the king and said, “See now, your servant has sheep shearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant.”38✦ 25 The king said to Absalom, “No, my son, let’s not all go, lest we be burdensome to you.” He pressed him; however he would not go, but blessed him.39✦ 26 Then Absalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us.” The king said to him, “Why should he go with you?”40✦ 27 But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.41✦ 28 Absalom commanded his servants, saying, “Mark now, when Amnon’s heart42 is merry with wine; and when I tell you, ‘Strike Amnon,’ then kill him. Don’t be afraid. Haven’t I commanded you? Be courageous, and be valiant!”4344✦ 29 The servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had comman45ded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man got up on his mule and fled.46✦ 30 While they were on the way, the news came to David, saying, “Absalom has slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left!”47 31 Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth48; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.49✦ 32 Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answered, “Don’t let my lord50 suppose that they have killed all the young men, the king’s sons, for Amnon only is dead; for by the appointment of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.51 33 Now therefore don’t let my lord52 the king take the thing to his heart53, to think that all the king’s sons are dead; for only Amnon is dead.”54 34 But Absalom fled. The young man55 who kept the watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming by way of the hillside behind him.56 35 Jonadab said to the king, “Behold, the king’s sons are coming! It is as your servant said.”57 36 As soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voices and wept. The king also and all his servants wept bitterly.58 37 But Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.59✦ 38 So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.60 39 King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.

121 Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart3 was toward Absalom.4 2 Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman56 from there, and said to her, “Please act like a mourner, and put on mourning clothing, please, and don’t anoint yourself with oil; but be as a woman who has mourned a long time for the dead.7✦ 3 Go in to the king and speak like this to him.” So Joab put the words in her mouth.8 4 When the woman9 of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground10, showed respect, and said, “Help, O king!”11 5 The king said to her, “What ails you?” She answered, “Truly I am a widow, and my husband is dead.1213✦ 6 Your servant had two sons; and they both fought together in the field, and there was no one to part them, but the one struck the other and killed him.14✦ 7 Behold, the whole family has risen against your servant, and they say, ‘Deliver him who struck his brother, that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he killed, and so destroy the heir also.’ Thus they would quench my coal which is left, and would leave to my husband neither name nor remainder on the surface of the earth15.”1617✦ 8 The king said to the woman18, “Go to your house, and I will give a command concerning you.”19 9 The woman20 of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord21, O king, may the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house; and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”22 10 The king said, “Whoever says anything to you, bring him to me, and he will not bother you any more.”23 11 Then she said, “Please let the king remember Yahweh your God24, that the avenger of blood25 destroy not any more, lest they destroy my son.” He said, “As Yahweh lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the earth26.”2728 12 Then the woman29 said, “Please let your servant speak a word to my lord30 the king.” He said, “Say on.”31 13 The woman32 said, “Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God33? For in speaking this word the king is as one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring home again his banished one.34 14 For we must die, and are like water35 spilled on the ground36, which can’t be gathered up again; neither does God37 take away life, but devises means, that he who is banished not be an outcast from him.38✦ 15 Now therefore, seeing that I have come to speak this word to my lord39 the king, it is because the people have made me afraid. Your servant said, ‘I will now speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.’40 16 For the king will hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man41 who would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God42.43 17 Then your servant said, ‘Please let the word of my lord44 the king bring rest; for as an angel of God45, so is my lord the king to discern good46 and bad. May Yahweh, your God, be with you.’”47✦ 18 Then the king answered the woman48, “Please don’t hide anything from me that I ask you.” The woman said, “Let my lord49 the king now speak.”50 19 The king said, “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?” The woman51 answered, “As your soul52 lives, my lord53 the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab urged me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your servant.54 20 Your servant Joab has done this thing to change the face of the matter. My lord55 is wise, according to the wisdom56 of an angel of God57, to know all things that are in the earth58.”59✦ 21 The king said to Joab, “Behold now, I have granted this thing. Go therefore, and bring the young man60 Absalom back.”61 22 Joab fell to the ground62 on his face, showed respect, and blessed the king. Joab said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord63, O king, in that the king has performed the request of his servant.”64✦ 23 So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.65 24 The king said, “Let him return to his own house, but let him not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, and didn’t see the king’s face.66 25 Now in all Israel there was no one to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.67 26 When he cut the hair of his head (now it was at every year’s end that he cut it; because it was heavy on him, therefore he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels68, after the king’s weight.69✦ 27 Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar. She was a woman70 with a beautiful face.71 28 Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, and he didn’t see the king’s face. 29 Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. Then he sent again a second time, but he would not come.72 30 Therefore he said to his servants, “Behold, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.73✦ 31 Then Joab arose and came to Absalom to his house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my field on fire?”74 32 Absalom answered Joab, “Behold, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, that I may send you to the king, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still. Now therefore, let me see the king’s face; and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”’”7576 33 So Joab came to the king and told him; and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground77 before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.

11 After this, Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.2✦ 2 Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. When any man3 had a suit which should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him, and said, “What city are you from?” He said, “Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.”4✦ 3 Absalom said to him, “Behold, your matters are good5 and right; but there is no man6 deputized by the king to hear you.”7✦ 4 Absalom said moreover, “Oh that I were made judge in the land8, that every man9 who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!”10✦ 5 It was so, that when any man11 came near to bow down to him, he stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and kissed him.12✦ 6 Absalom did this sort of thing to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.13✦ 7 At the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to Yahweh, in Hebron.1415✦ 8 For your servant vowed a vow while I stayed at Geshur in Syria, saying, ‘If Yahweh shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I will serve Yahweh.’”161718✦ 9 The king said to him, “Go in peace19.” So he arose and went to Hebron.20 10 But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron!’”21✦ 11 Two hundred men went with Absalom out of Jerusalem, who were invited, and went in their simplicity; and they didn’t know anything.22 12 Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy was strong, for the people increased continually with Absalom.23 13 A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.”24 14 David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, “Arise! Let’s flee, or else none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry to depart, lest he overtake us quickly and bring down evil on us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”25 15 The king’s servants said to the king, “Behold, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord26 the king chooses.”27 16 The king went out, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.28 17 The king went out, and all the people after him; and they stayed in Beth Merhak.29 18 All his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.30 19 Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why do you also go with us? Return, and stay with the king; for you are a foreigner and also an exile. Return to your own place.31 20 Whereas you came but yesterday, should I today make you go up and down with us, since I go where I may? Return, and take back your brothers. Mercy and truth be with you.”3233 21 Ittai answered the king and said, “As Yahweh lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in what place my lord the king is, whether for death or for life, your servant will be there also34.”3536 22 David said to Ittai, “Go and pass over.” Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.37 23 All the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness.3839✦ 24 Behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant40 of God41; and they set down God’s ark; and Abiathar went up until all the people finished passing out of the city.42✦ 25 The king said to Zadok, “Carry God43’s ark back into the city. If I find favor in Yahweh’s eyes, he will bring me again, and show me both it and his habitation;4445 26 but if he says, ‘I have no delight in you,’ behold, here I am. Let him do to me as seems good46 to him.”47✦ 27 The king said also to Zadok the priest, “Aren’t you a seer? Return into the city in peace48, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.49✦ 28 Behold, I will stay at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”50 29 Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried God51’s ark to Jerusalem again; and they stayed there.52 30 David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives53, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered and went barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.5455✦ 31 Someone told David, saying, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” David said, “Yahweh, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness56.”5758 32 When David had come to the top, where God59 was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his tunic torn and earth60 on his head.6162✦ 33 David said to him, “If you pass on with me, then you will be a burden to me;63✦ 34 but if you return to the city, and tell Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king. As I have been your father’s servant in time past, so I will now be your servant; then will you defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.’64✦ 35 Don’t you have Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Therefore whatever you hear out of the king’s house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.65 36 Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son. Send to me everything that you shall hear by them.”66 37 So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city; and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

11 When David was a little past the top, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a couple of donkeys saddled, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a container of wine.2✦ 2 The king said to Ziba, “What do you mean by these?” Ziba said, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that those who are faint in the wilderness may drink.”3✦ 3 The king said, “Where is your master’s son?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem; for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore me the kingdom of my father.’”4✦ 4 Then the king said to Ziba, “Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” Ziba said, “I bow down. Let me find favor in your sight, my lord5, O king.”6✦ 5 When King David came to Bahurim, behold, a man7 of the family of Saul’s house came out, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera. He came out and cursed as he came.8✦ 6 He cast stones at David and at all the servants of King David, and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.9 7 Shimei said when he cursed, “Be gone, be gone, you man10 of blood, and wicked fellow!11✦ 8 Yahweh has returned on you all the blood12 of Saul’s house, in whose place you have reigned! Yahweh has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son! Behold, you are caught by your own mischief, because you are a man13 of blood!”1415✦ 9 Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord16 the king? Please let me go over and take off his head.”17✦ 10 The king said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Because he curses, and because Yahweh has said to him18, ‘Curse David,’ who then shall say, ‘Why have you done so?’”1920✦ 11 David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my son, who came out of my bowels, seeks my life. How much more this Benjamite, now? Leave him alone, and let him curse; for Yahweh has invited him.2122✦ 12 It may be that Yahweh will look on the wrong done to me, and that Yahweh will repay me good23 for the cursing of me today.”2425✦ 13 So David and his men went by the way; and Shimei went along on the hillside opposite him and cursed as he went, threw stones at him, and threw dust26.27 14 The king and all the people who were with him arrived weary; and he refreshed himself there.28 15 Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.29 16 When Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, had come to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”3031✦ 17 Absalom said to Hushai, “Is this your kindness to your friend? Why didn’t you go with your friend?”32 18 Hushai said to Absalom, “No; but whomever Yahweh and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, I will be his, and I will stay with him.3334 19 Again, whom should I serve? Shouldn’t I serve in the presence of his son? As I have served in your father’s presence, so I will be in your presence.”35 20 Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give your counsel what we shall do.”36 21 Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Go in to your father37’s concubines that he has left to keep the house. Then all Israel will hear that you are abhorred by your father. Then the hands of all who are with you will be strong.”38 22 So they spread a tent for Absalom on the top of the house, and Absalom went in to his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.39✦ 23 The counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in those days, was as if a man40 inquired at the inner sanctuary of God41. All the counsel of Ahithophel was like this both with David and with Absalom.

121 Moreover Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me now choose twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David tonight.3✦ 2 I will come on him while he is weary and exhausted, and will make him afraid. All the people who are with him will flee. I will strike the king only,4 3 and I will bring back all the people to you. The man5 whom you seek is as if all returned. All the people shall be in peace6.”7 4 The saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.8 5 Then Absalom said, “Now call Hushai the Archite also, and let’s hear likewise what he says.”9 6 When Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom spoke to him, saying, “Ahithophel has spoken like this. Shall we do what he says? If not, speak up.”10✦ 7 Hushai said to Absalom, “The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good11.”12✦ 8 Hushai said moreover, “You know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are fierce in their minds, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Your father is a man13 of war, and will not lodge with the people.14✦ 9 Behold, he is now hidden in some pit, or in some other place. It will happen, when some of them have fallen at the first, that whoever hears it will say, ‘There is a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!’15✦ 10 Even he who is valiant, whose heart16 is as the heart of a lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man17, and those who are with him are valiant men.18✦ 11 But I counsel that all Israel be gathered together to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that you go to battle in your own person.19✦ 12 So we will come on him in some place where he will be found, and we will light20 on him as the dew falls on the ground21, then we will not leave so much as one of him and of all the men who are with him.22✦ 13 Moreover, if he has gone into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there isn’t one small stone found there.”23✦ 14 Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel.” For Yahweh had ordained to defeat the good24 counsel of Ahithophel25, to the intent that Yahweh might bring evil on Absalom.2627✦ 15 Then Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, “Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel that way; and I have counseled this way.28✦ 16 Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, ‘Don’t lodge tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but by all means pass over, lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people who are with him.’”29 17 Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying by En Rogel; and a female servant used to go and report to them, and they went and told King David; for they couldn’t risk being seen coming into the city.3031 18 But a boy saw them, and told Absalom. By the morning light42 there lacked not one of them who had not gone over the Jordan.43 23 When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey, arose, and went home to his city, set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and was buried in the tomb of his father.45✦ 24 Then David came to Mahanaim. Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.46 25 Absalom set Amasa over the army instead of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man47 whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.4849✦ 26 Israel and Absalom encamped in the land50 of Gilead.51 27 When David had come to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,52535455✦ 28 brought beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, meal, parched grain, beans, lentils, roasted grain,5657✦ 29 honey, butter, sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David and for the people who were with him to eat; for they said, “The people are hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness.”

1✦1 David counted the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.2✦ 2 David sent the people out, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, “I will also surely go out with you myself.”3✦ 3 But the people said, “You shall not go out, for if we flee away, they will not care for us, neither if half of us die, will they care for us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. Therefore now it is better that you are ready to help us out of the city.”4 4 The king said to them, “I will do what seems best to you.” The king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.✦ 5 The king comman5ded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom.” All the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.6✦ 6 So the people went out into the field against Israel; and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.7✦ 7 The people of Israel were struck there before David’s servants, and there was a great slaughter there that day of twenty thousand men.8✦ 8 For the battle was there spread over the surface of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.9✦ 9 Absalom happened to meet David’s servants. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak; and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was hanging between the sky and earth10; and the mule that was under him went on.1112✦ 10 A certain man13 saw it, and told Joab, and said, “Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak.”14✦ 11 Joab said to the man15 who told him, “Behold, you saw it, and why didn’t you strike him there to the ground16? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a sash.”17✦ 12 The man18 said to Joab, “Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I still wouldn’t stretch out my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, ‘Beware that no one touch the young man Absalom.’19✦ 13 Otherwise, if I had dealt falsely against his life (and there is no matter hidden from the king), then you yourself would have set yourself against me.”2021 14 Then Joab said, “I’m not going to wait like this with you.” He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart22 while he was still alive in the middle of the oak.23✦ 15 Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom, and killed him.24 16 Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held the people back.25 17 They took Absalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. Then all Israel fled, each to his own tent.26 18 Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar which is in the king’s valley, for he said, “I have no son to keep my name in memory.” He called the pillar after his own name. It is called Absalom’s monument, to this day.27✦ 19 Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Let me now run and carry the king news, how Yahweh has avenged him of his enemies.”2829 20 Joab said to him, “You must not be the bearer of news today, but you must carry news another day. But today you must carry no news, because the king’s son is dead.”30 21 Then Joab said to the Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen!” The Cushite bowed himself to Joab, and ran.31 22 Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, “But come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite.” Joab said, “Why do you want to run, my son, since you will have no reward for the news?”32 23 “But come what may,” he said, “I will run.” He said to him, “Run!” Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.33 24 Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman34 went up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.3536✦ 25 The watchman shouted and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is news in his mouth.” He came closer and closer.37✦ 26 The watchman38 saw another man running; and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, “Behold, a man running alone!” The king said, “He also brings news.”3940✦ 27 The watchman41 said, “I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” The king said, “He is a good42 man, and comes with good news.”43✦ 28 Ahimaaz called, and said to the king, “All is well.” He bowed himself before the king with his face to the earth44, and said, “Blessed is Yahweh your God45, who has delivered up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king!”4647 29 The king said, “Is it well with the young man48 Absalom?” Ahimaaz answered, “When Joab sent the king’s servant, even me your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I don’t know what it was.”49 30 The king said, “Come and stand here.” He came and stood still.50 31 Behold, the Cushite came. The Cushite said, “Good news for my lord51 the king, for Yahweh has avenged you today of all those who rose up against you.”52 32 The king said to the Cushite, “Is it well with the young man53 Absalom?” The Cushite answered, “May the enemies of my lord54 the king, and all who rise up against you to do you harm, be as that young man is.”5556 33 The king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate and wept. As he went, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!57 I wish I had died instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son58!”

12✦1 Joab was told, “Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.” 3 2The victory that day was turned into mourning among all the people, for the people heard it said that day, “The king grieves for his son.”4 3 The people sneaked into the city that day, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.5 4 The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, “My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!”6✦ 5 Joab came into the house to the king, and said, “Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants7 who today have saved your life, and the lives of your sons and of your daughters, and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines;8 6 in that you love those who hate you and hate those who love you. For you have declared today that princes and servants are nothing to you. For today I perceive that if Absalom had lived and we had all died today, then it would have pleased you well.9 7 Now therefore arise, go out and speak to comfort your servants; for I swear by Yahweh, if you don’t go out, not a man will stay with you this night. That would be worse to you than all the evil that has happened to you from your youth until now.”1011✦ 8 Then the king arose and sat in the gate. The people were all told, “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” All the people came before the king. Now therefore why don’t you speak a word of bringing the king back?” 11 King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, “Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house, since the speech of all Israel has come to the king, to return him to his house?16✦ 12 You are my brothers. I say, you and Ziba divide the land51.”52 30 Mephibosheth said to the king, “Yes, let him take all, because my lord53 the king has come in peace54 to his own house.”55 31 Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim; and he went over the Jordan with the king to conduct him over the Jordan.56✦ 32 Now Barzillai was a very aged man57, even eighty years old. 11 There was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year; and David sought the face of Yahweh. With the perfect man52 you will show yourself perfect.53 27 With the pure you will show yourself pure. With the crooked you will show yourself shrewd. 28 You will save the afflicted people, but your eyes are on the arrogant, that you may bring them down. 29 For you are my lamp, Yahweh. Yahweh will light up my darkness54.555657✦ 30 For by you, I run against a troop. By my God58, I leap over a wall. 31 As for God59, his way is perfect. Yahweh’s word is tested. He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him.60616263 32 For who is God64, besides Yahweh? Who is a rock, besides our God?6566 3367 God is my strong fortress. 11 Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he had heard that they had anointed2 him king in the place of his father, and Hiram had always loved David.3 ✦2 Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,4 3 “You know that David my father could not build a house for the name of Yahweh his God5 because of the wars which were around him on every side, until Yahweh put his enemies under the soles of his feet.67 ✦4 But now Yahweh my God8 has given me rest on every side. There is no enemy and no evil occurrence.91011 5 Behold, I intend to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God12, as Yahweh spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place shall build the house for my name.’1314 ✦6 Now therefore command that cedar trees be cut for me out of Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants; and I will give you wages for your servants according to all that you say. For you know that there is nobody among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”15 ✦7 When Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly, and said, “Blessed is Yahweh today, who has given to David a wise son to rule over this great people.”1617 ✦8 Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, “I have heard the message which you have sent to me. ↩ ◇ Note. Jerusalem captured. What Joshua 15:63 admitted Israel had failed to do, David finally accomplishes. Jerusalem becomes the City of David — politically neutral (between Judah and the northern tribes), militarily defensible, and (after the Ark’s arrival in ch 6 and Solomon’s temple in 1 Kgs 6) cosmically central. Recent excavation in the City of David (Eilat Mazar’s "Large Stone Structure") has produced a candidate for David’s palace, though identification remains debated. The conquest of Jerusalem is the foundational event of biblical Israel in its biblical form.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). CART a vehicle moving on wheels, and usually drawn by oxen (2 Samuel 6:3). The Hebrew word thus rendered, ’agalah (1 Samuel 6:7, 8), is also rendered “wagon” (Genesis 45:19). It is used also to denote a war-chariot (Psalm 46:9). Carts were used for the removal of the ark and its sacred utensils (Numbers 7:3, 6). After retaining the ark amongst them for seven months, the Philistines sent it back to the Israelites. On this occasion they set it in a new cart, probably a rude construction, with solid wooden wheels like that still used in Western Asia, which was drawn by two milch cows, which conveyed it straight to Beth-shemesh. A “cart rope,” for the purpose of fastening loads on carts, is used (Isaiah 5:18) as a symbol of the power of sinful pleasures or habits over him who indulges them. (See CORD.) In Syria and Palestine wheel-carriages for any other purpose than the conveyance of agricultural produce are almost unknown.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). CYMBALS (Hebrews tzeltzelim, from a root meaning to “tinkle”), musical instruments, consisting of two convex pieces of brass one held in each hand, which were clashed together to produce a loud clanging sound; castanets; “loud cymbals.” “Highsounding cymbals” consisted of two larger plates, one held also in each hand (2 Samuel 6:5; Psalm 150:5; 1 Chronicles 13:8; 15:16, 19, 28; 1 Corinthians 13:1).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). FIR the uniform rendering in the Authorized Version (marg. R.V., “cypress”) of berosh (2 Samuel 6:5; 1 Kings 5:8, 10; 6:15, 34; 9:11, etc.), a lofty tree (Isaiah 55:13) growing on Lebanon (37:24). Its wood was used in making musical instruments and doors of houses, and for ceilings (2 Chronicles 3:5), the decks of ships (Ezekiel 27:5), floorings and spear-shafts (Nah. 2:3, R.V.). The true fir (abies) is not found in Palestine, but the pine tree, of which there are four species, is common. The precise kind of tree meant by the “green fir tree” (Hos. 14:8) is uncertain. Some regard it as the sherbin tree, a cypress resembling the cedar; others, the Aleppo or maritime pine (Pinus halepensis), which resembles the Scotch fir; while others think that the “stone-pine” (Pinus pinea) is probably meant. (See PINE.)

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). FATLING (1.) A fatted animal for slaughter (2 Samuel 6:13; Isaiah 11:6; Ezekiel 39:18. Comp. Matthew 22:4, where the word used in the original, sitistos, means literally “corn-fed;” i.e., installed, fat). (2.) Psalm 66:15 (Hebrews meah, meaning “marrowy,” “fat,” a species of sheep). (3.) 1 Samuel 15:9 (Hebrews mishneh, meaning “the second,” and hence probably “cattle of a second quality,” or lambs of the second birth, i.e., autmnal lambs, and therfore of less value).

↩ ⌘ Hebrew. M’karker (מְכַרְכֵּר). A rare verb (only here and 6:16) — likely intensive whirling or leaping. David is described as wearing only a linen ephod (a priestly garment), an extraordinary embodiment of priestly-royal fusion. Michal’s contempt (6:20–23) and David’s defiant response ("I will be even more contemptible than this," 6:22) mark the moment Saul’s daughter is finally cut off from the Davidic future — and from any further child-bearing role (6:23). The chapter records both the high point of David’s religious devotion and the final closure of the Saulide line through Michal.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). NATHAN given. (1.) A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chronicles 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Samuel 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 11, 22-45). His two sons, Zabad (1 Chronicles 2:36) and Azariah (1 Kings 4:5) occupied places of honour at the king’s court. He last appears in assisting David in reorganizing the public worship (2 Chronicles 29:25). He seems to have written a life of David, and also a life of Solomon (1 Chronicles 29:29; 2 Chronicles 9:29). (2.) A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Samuel 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31). (3.) Ezra 8:16.

↩ ◇ Note. The Davidic Covenant. The pivot of OT theology: an unconditional dynastic promise. Forever commits Yahweh to a perpetual Davidic line. When the line is interrupted at the exile, the promise becomes the engine of messianic expectation — a future Davidic king will fulfill what the historical kings failed to embody. Heb 1:5 and Acts 2:30 cite this verse as messianic; the NT places Jesus in the Davidic line precisely to claim its fulfillment. Modern scholarship reads the covenant as foundational to both Jewish messianism and Christian christology.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). TEKOA , TEKOAH pitching of tents; fastening down, a town of Judah, about 12 miles south of Jerusalem, and visible from the city. From this place Joab procured a “wise woman,” who pretended to be in great affliction, and skilfully made her case known to David. Her address to the king was in the form of an apologue, similar to that of Nathan (2 Samuel 12:1-6). The object of Joab was, by the intervention of this woman, to induce David to bring back Absalom to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 14:2, 4, 9). This was also the birth-place of the prophet Amos (1:1). It is now the village of Teku’a, on the top of a hill among ruins, 5 miles south of Bethlehem, and close to Beth-haccerem (“Herod’s mountain”).

↩ ◇ Note. Nathan’s parable. One of the great moral set-pieces of scripture. Nathan tells David a parable of a rich man who steals a poor man’s ewe lamb; David, outraged, demands judgment; Nathan turns the parable on him. The structure — get the audience to convict themselves before revealing the indictment — is a powerful rhetorical form, used again by Joab via the wise woman of Tekoa in 14:1–20, and by Jesus in several parables (the two debtors, Luke 7:41–47). Few prophetic confrontations are as economically devastating.

↩ ◇ Note. David’s confession. The traditional superscription of Psalm 51 ("when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba") attaches that great penitential psalm to this moment. The brevity of the confession here — five Hebrew words, ḥata’ti laYHWH — contrasts with the elaborate structure of the psalm and with the lengthy Saulite excuse-making (1 Sam 15). The Davidic narrative gives us the principle: the great king is the one who admits the sin without qualification.

↩ ◇ Note. Tamar’s rape. Phyllis Trible’s reading in Texts of Terror remains influential: the narrative refuses to look away from the violence done to Tamar, and its placement immediately after Nathan’s "the sword shall never depart from your house" oracle (12:10) presents Amnon’s crime as the first installment of the Davidic curse. David’s silent fury (13:21 — "but he did nothing") becomes the moral and political vacuum that Absalom fills. The chapter is one of the OT’s starkest portraits of paternal failure following royal sin.

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). GESHUR bridge, the name of a district or principality of Syria near Gilead, between Mount Hermon and the Lake of Tiberias (2 Samuel 15:8; 1 Chronicles 2:23). The Geshurites probably inhabited the rocky fastness of Argob, the modern Lejah, in the north-east corner of Bashan. In the time of David it was ruled by Talmai, whose daughter he married, and who was the mother of Absalom, who fled to Geshur after the murder of Amnon (2 Samuel 13:37).

↩ ⌂ Easton. Dictionary (Easton's). KIDRON = Kedron = Cedron, turbid, the winter torrent which flows through the Valley of Jehoshaphat, on the eastern side of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives. This valley is known in Scripture only by the name “the brook Kidron.” David crossed this brook bare-foot and weeping, when fleeing from Absalom (2 Samuel 15:23, 30), and it was frequently crossed by our Lord in his journeyings to and fro (John 18:1). Here Asa burned the obscene idols of his mother (1 Kings 15:13), and here Athaliah was executed (2 Kings 11:16). It afterwards became the receptacle for all manner of impurities (2 Chronicles 29:16; 30:14); and in the time of Josiah this valley was the common cemetery of the city (2 Kings 23:6; comp. Jeremiah 26:23). Through this mountain ravine no water runs, except after heavy rains in the mountains round about Jerusalem. Its length from its head to en-Rogel is 2 3/4 miles. Its precipitous, rocky banks are filled with ancient tombs, especially the left bank opposite the temple area. The greatest desire of the Jews is to be buried there, from the idea that the Kidron is the “valley of Jehoshaphat” mentioned in Joel 3:2. Below en-Rogel the Kidron has no historical or sacred interest. It runs in a winding course through the wilderness of Judea to the north-western shore of the Dead Sea. Its whole length, in a straight line, is only some 20 miles, but in this space its descent is about 3,912 feet. (See KEDRON.) Recent excavations have brought to light the fact that the old bed of the Kidron is about 40 feet lower than its present bed, and about 70 feet nearer the sanctuary wall.

↩ ◇ Note. David flees Jerusalem. The king crosses the Kidron, ascends the Mount of Olives barefoot and weeping. The geography and posture become typologically significant: Jesus will cross the same Kidron and weep on the same Mount of Olives in Luke 19, Matt 26, John 18 — frequently read by patristic and medieval interpreters as deliberate Davidic typology. The Absalom rebellion is the structural inverse of David’s rise: the king now flees rather than ascends, the people he led now follow another, his counselor Ahithophel now sides with his son.

↩ ◇ Note. David’s psalm. 2 Sam 22 is preserved nearly verbatim as Psalm 18 — one of the few cases where the same poem appears in two biblical books. Minor textual variations between the two versions are studied by textual critics as a case study in how biblical poetry was transmitted. The placement here — late in David’s life, as a retrospective of deliverance — gives the psalm a different framing than the Psalter’s liturgical context. The dual preservation is rare and theologically significant: the same prayer functions both as David’s personal song and as Israel’s communal liturgy.

↩ ◇ Note. "The last words of David." A poetic oracle (23:2–7) where David speaks as a prophet — "the Spirit of Yahweh spoke through me" (23:2). The poem articulates the ideal of just kingship under God: "one who rules over men righteously, who rules in the fear of God, is as the light of the morning" (23:3–4). After David’s catastrophic moral failures earlier in the book, the ideal is voiced by him as both confession and aspiration. The placement frames the Davidic legacy not by what was achieved but by what was glimpsed.

↩ ◇ Note. The future Temple site. 2 Chr 3:1 identifies Araunah’s threshing floor as the site of Solomon’s temple — and traditionally as Mount Moriah (Gen 22:2), where Abraham bound Isaac. Three of the OT’s most sacred narratives — the Akedah, David’s plague-stayed altar, Solomon’s temple — are concentrated on the same patch of ground. The Temple Mount of modern Jerusalem is the same site, contested across three Abrahamic traditions. The book of 2 Samuel ends not with Solomon’s succession (which 1 Kings narrates) but with this sacred geography, sealing the link between David’s reign and the Temple to come.
